grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 0: 英えい語ごの 語ご順じゅん
grammarPoints.title: English Word Order
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 英えい語ごの 文ぶんの 基き本ほん的てきな 語ご順じゅんは、〈 **主しゅ語ご** （…は・が） ＋ **動どう詞し** （…する・です） ＋ その他たの語ご句く 〉です。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: English sentences follow a fixed word order based on the function of the words, which differs from Japanese word order. The basic English word order is: 〈 **Subject** (… is/has/does) + **Verb** (… to be/do) + Other phrases 〉.

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 1: be動どう詞しと 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し
grammarPoints.title: **I am** Edward Trout. / **I like** Japanese sweets.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
be動どう詞し（I am...）：amは 前ぜん後ごの 言こと葉ばを つなぐ 役やく割わりで、be動どう詞しと いう。I amは I’mと 短たん縮しゅくする ことが できる。
一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（I like...）：動どう作さや 状じょう態たいを 表あらわす 場ば合あいは、主しゅ語ごの 後うしろに playや likeなどの 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞しが 入はいる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Be-verb (am/is/are): The verb 'am' connects the words before and after it [1]. 'I am' can be contracted to 'I'm' [1]. General Verb (play/like): When expressing actions or states, a general verb like 'play' or 'like' is placed after the subject [1]. In the present tense, be-verbs and general verbs are not used together [2].

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 1: be動どう詞しと 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し
grammarPoints.title: **Do you like** comics? / **I do not like** comics.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（否ひ定てい文ぶんと疑ぎ問もん文ぶん）：疑ぎ問もん文ぶんで、たずねる 場ば合あいは、文ぶんの はじめに Doを 置おき、文ぶん末まつを 上あげる [3]。否ひ定てい文ぶんでは、動どう詞しの 前まえに do not [don’t]が 入はいる [3]。話はなし言こと葉ばでは don’tを 使つかう ことが 多おおいが、強つよく 否ひ定ていする 場ば合あいや 書かき言こと葉ばでは do notを 使つかう [4].
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: For questions using a general verb, place 'Do' at the beginning and raise intonation at the end [3]. For negation, 'do not' is placed before the main verb [3]. 'Don't' is common in speech, but 'do not' is used for emphasis or in writing [4].

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 2: 疑ぎ問もん詞し
grammarPoints.title: **What is** that? / **Who is** your favorite character?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し：あるものが 何なにかを たずねる ときは whatを [5]、ある人ひとが だれなのかを たずねる ときは whoを 使つかう [5]。疑問詞には、what、when、where、who、howなどが あります [6]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Interrogative words (What, Who, When, Where, How, etc.) are used to ask specific information [6]. Use 'what' to ask what something is [5], and 'who' to ask who someone is [5]. These words typically start the question [6].

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 3: 名めい詞し
grammarPoints.title: **How many rabbits do you have**?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 名めい詞し（数かずえ方かた）：人ひとや ものの 名な前まえを 表あらわす 語ごを 名めい詞しと いう [7]。2ふたり人以い上じょうの 人ひとや 2つ以い上じょうの ものは、多おおくの 場ば合あい、名めい詞しに sまたは esを つける [8, 9]。数かずえられない 名めい詞し（water、meatなど）は a[an]が ついたり、sで 終おわる 形かたちにはならない [7]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Nouns name people or things [7]. Countable nouns (two or more) usually take the plural form (-s or -es) [8, 9]. Uncountable nouns (materials, abstract things) do not take 'a/an' or typically use the plural form ending in -s [7].

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 4: 三さん人称にんしょう単たん数すう現げん在ざい形けい
grammarPoints.title: **Fumiya lives** in Hawaii. / **Does Fumiya live** near a beach? / **Maria does not speak** Japanese.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 三さん人称にんしょう単たん数すう現げん在ざい形けい：主しゅ語ごが I、you以い外がいで 単たん数すうの 場ば合あい、動どう詞しを sまたは esで 終おわる 形かたちに する [10, 11]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは doesを 主しゅ語ごの 前まえに 置おき、動どう詞しに s、esを つけない [11, 12]。否ひ定てい文ぶんは does not [doesn't]を 動どう詞しの 前まえに 入いれ、動どう詞しに s、esを つけない [11, 13]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When the subject is third person singular, the verb takes -s or -es in affirmatives [10, 11]. For questions, use 'does' before the subject (verb is base form) [11, 12]. For negation, use 'does not/doesn't' before the verb (verb is base form) [11, 13].
examples: **Does he go** to the beach every day?

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 5: 代だい名めい詞し
grammarPoints.title: **Do you know him**? / **Whose ticket is this**? **It is mine**.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 代だい名めい詞し：一いち度ど 話わ題だいに 出でた 名めい詞しのかわりを する 語ごを 代だい名めい詞しと いう [14]。人ひとや ものを 動どう詞しの あとに 続つづけて「…を、…に」と 言いう ときは，me（私わたし）、you（あなた(たち)）、him（彼かれ）、her（彼かの女じょ）、them（彼かれら・彼かの女じょら・それら）を 使つかう [15].
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Pronouns replace nouns already mentioned [14]. Use objective pronouns (me, him, her, them) after a verb ('to whom,' 'who/what is affected') [15]. Possessive pronouns (mine, yours) are used to indicate ownership [16].
examples: **That is Anna. Do you know her?**
**Whose bag is this? It is mine.**

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 6: 現げん在ざい進しん行こう形けい
grammarPoints.title: **I am watching** TV now. / **Are you walking** around a lake? / **What are people doing**?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい進しん行こう形けい：〈am [are, is] ＋ ...ing〉の 形かたちを 現げん在ざい進しん行こう形けいと いい、「...」の 動どう作さが ちょうど 今いま 進しん行こうしている ことを 表あらわす [17, 18]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは、am、are、isを 主しゅ語ごの 前まえに 置おく [19].
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) expresses an action happening right now [17, 18]. For questions, invert the subject and the be-verb (Are you...?) [19].

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 7: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し の 過か去こ形けい
grammarPoints.title: **I stayed** in Canada last winter. / **I went** to Canada during the winter vacation.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（過か去こ形けい 肯こう定てい）：すでに 終おわった ことを 表あらわす 場ば合あい、動どう詞しを 過か去こ形けいに する [20, 21]。規き則そく動どう詞しは edで 終おわり、不ふ規き則そく動どう詞しは 変へん化かする (went, saw, ateなど) [20].
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To describe completed actions in the past, use the past tense form of the verb [20, 21]. Regular verbs add -ed, while irregular verbs change forms (e.g., go -> went) [20].

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 7: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し の 過か去こ形けい
grammarPoints.title: **Did you eat** rice cakes? / **I did not buy** a good luck charm.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 過か去こ形けい 疑ぎ問もん文ぶんと 否ひ定てい文ぶん：疑ぎ問もん文ぶんで、主しゅ語ごの 前まえに didを 置おき [22]，動どう詞しは 過か去こ形けいに しない [22]。否ひ定てい文ぶんは 動どう詞しの 前まえに did not [didn’t]を 置おく [23]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: For past tense questions, place 'did' before the subject (verb is base form) [22]. For negative statements, place 'did not/didn't' before the verb (verb is base form) [23].
examples: **I did not buy** a good luck charm.

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 8: be動どう詞し の 過か去こ形けいと 過か去こ進しん行こう形けい
grammarPoints.title: **Were you nervous** during the contest?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: be動どう詞し（過か去こ形けい）：amや isの 過か去こ形けいは wasに、areの 過か去こ形けいは wereに なる [24]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは be動どう詞し 過か去こ形けいを 主しゅ語ごの 前まえに 置おく [24]。was notは wasn’tに、were notは weren’tに 短たん縮しゅくできる [24].
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The past tense of 'am/is' is 'was'; 'are' is 'were' [24]. Questions are formed by placing the past tense be-verb before the subject [24]. Contractions (wasn't, weren't) can be used for negation [24].

grammarPoints.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 8: be動どう詞し の 過か去こ形けいと 過か去こ進しん行こう形けい
grammarPoints.title: **I was playing** soccer then.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 過か去こ進しん行こう形けい：過か去この ある 時じ点てんに していた ことを 表あらわすには、〈was [were] + ...ing〉を 使つかう [25, 26]。この 形かたちを 過か去こ進しん行こう形けいと いう [25].
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The past continuous form (was/were + -ing) expresses an action that was in progress at a specific point in the past [25, 26].
examples: **I was playing** the guitar at 7 p.m. yesterday.

grammarPoints.title: **I am** Edward Trout.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: be動どう詞し（I am...）：amは 前ぜん後ごの 言こと葉ばを つなぐ 役やく割わりで、be動どう詞しと いう。I amは I’mと 短たん縮しゅくする ことが できる [1]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The verb 'am' acts as a be-verb, connecting the words before and after it [1]. 'I am' can be contracted to 'I'm' [1]. This is used to state identity or status.

grammarPoints.title: I **like** Japanese sweets.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（肯こう定てい文）：動どう作さや 状じょう態たいを 表あらわす 場ば合あいは、主しゅ語ごの 後うしろに playや likeなどの 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞しが 入はいる [1]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When expressing actions or states, a general verb such as 'play' or 'like' is placed after the subject [1]. This is used to express habitual actions or current states.

grammarPoints.title: **Do you like** comics?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（疑ぎ問もん文）：たずねる 場ば合あいは、文ぶんの はじめに Doを 置おき、文ぶん末まつを 上あげる [3]。答こたえる ときは Yes, I do. または No, I do not [don't]. [3]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To ask a question using a general verb, place 'Do' at the beginning of the sentence and raise the intonation at the end [3]. The response uses 'Yes, I do.' or 'No, I do not (don't).' [3].

grammarPoints.title: I **do not** like comics.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（否ひ定てい文）：否ひ定てい文ぶんでは、動どう詞しの 前まえに do notが くる [3]。話はなし言こと葉ばでは don’tを 使つかう ことが 多おおいですが、強つよく 否ひ定ていする 場ば合あいや 書かき言こと葉ばでは do notを 使つかいます [4]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: In negative sentences with general verbs, 'do not' is placed before the main verb [3]. In casual speech, 'don't' is often used, but 'do not' is used for strong negation or in writing [4].

grammarPoints.title: **Are you** an anime fan?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: be動どう詞し（疑ぎ問もん文）：相あい手てについて たずねる とき、be動どう詞しを 使つかった 文ぶんでは Are you ...?と 言いう。文ぶん末まつが 上あげ調ちょう子しに なる [27]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When asking about the listener using a be-verb, use 'Are you...?' [27]. The intonation rises at the end of the sentence. Responses use 'Yes, I am.' or 'No, I am not (I'm not).' [27].

grammarPoints.title: I **am not** an anime fan.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: be動どう詞し（否ひ定てい文）：否ひ定てい文ぶんでは、amの あとに notが くる [27]。I am notは I’m notと 短たん縮しゅく できる [27]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: In negative sentences with the be-verb 'am,' 'not' is placed after 'am' [27]. 'I am not' can be contracted to 'I'm not' [27].
examples: **No, I’m not.** I’m a baseball fan.

grammarPoints.title: This is Jun. **He is** in Class 1-1.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 代だい名めい詞し（he/she）：すでに 話わ題だいに なった 人ひとについて 言いう とき、男だん性せいは he、女じょ性せいは sheで 表あらわす [28]。あとに 続つづく be動どう詞しは isに なる [28]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When referring to a male person already mentioned, use 'he'; use 'she' for a female person [28]. The following be-verb is 'is' [28].

grammarPoints.title: **Is he** on the soccer team?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: be動どう詞し（疑ぎ問もん文）：たずねる ときは isを 文ぶんの はじめに 置おく [28]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To ask a question about a third person singular subject, place 'is' at the beginning of the sentence [28]. Responses use 'Yes, he is.' or 'No, he is not (isn't).' [29].

grammarPoints.title: I **can make** gyoza.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 助じょ動どう詞し（can）：can ...で 「…できる」という 意い味みになり、得とくいな ことや、できる ことなどを 表あらわす [30]。否ひ定てい文ぶんでは cannot [can’t]を 使つかう [30]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: 'Can' means 'to be able to...' and expresses ability or something one is good at [30]. The negative form is 'cannot' or 'can't' [30]. 'Can't' is common in speech, but 'cannot' is used for emphasis or in writing [31].
examples: My father **can make** gyoza very well.

grammarPoints.title: **Can you read** hiragana?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 助じょ動どう詞し（can 疑ぎ問もん文）：たずねる ときは canを 文ぶんの はじめに 置おく [30]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To ask a question using 'can,' place 'Can' at the beginning of the sentence [30]. Responses use 'Yes, I can.' or 'No, I cannot (can't).' [30].

grammarPoints.title: **This is** your pen. **That is** my pen.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 指し示じ代だい名めい詞し（This/That）：人ひとや ものを 指さす とき、近ちかければ thisで、離はなれていれば thatで 表あらわす [32]。あとに 続つづく be動どう詞しは isに なる [32]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use 'this' for something nearby and 'that' for something farther away [32]. The following be-verb is 'is' [32].

grammarPoints.title: **Is this** a bird?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 指し示じ代だい名めい詞し（疑ぎ問もん文/代だい名めい詞し it）：たずねる ときは isを 文ぶんの はじめに 置おく [32]。すでに 話わ題だいに なった ものについて 言いう ときは itで 表あらわす [32]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: For questions, place 'is' at the beginning [32]. When referring to a thing already mentioned, use 'it' [32].

grammarPoints.title: **What is** that?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し（What）：あるものが 何なにかを たずねる ときは whatを 使つかう [5]。疑問文ぎもんぶんであっても、whatが 主しゅ語ごの 役やく割わりをすると 見みなし、be動どう詞しを isで 受うける [5]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use 'what' to ask what something is [5]. The sentence structure follows the be-verb question pattern. When 'what' acts as the subject, the be-verb typically takes the 'is' form [5].
examples: **It is** a kamon, a symbol for a family.

grammarPoints.title: **Who is** your favorite character?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し（Who）：ある人ひとが だれなのかを たずねる ときは whoを 使つかう [5]。疑問文ぎもんぶんであっても、whoが 主しゅ語ごの 役やく割わりをする 場合ばあいは、be動どう詞しは isの 形かたちを とる [5]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use 'who' to ask who a person is [5]. When 'who' acts as the subject, the be-verb typically takes the 'is' form [5].

grammarPoints.title: **How do you come** to school?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し（How）：Howや whatの あとに 疑ぎ問もん文ぶんの 形かたちを 続つづける [33]。How do you ...?は、「どのように…しますか」と たずねる ときに 使つかう [33]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use 'How do you...?' to ask about the method or manner of an action [33]. The question word is followed by the interrogative form (Do you...) [33].

grammarPoints.title: **When do you come** to school?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し（When）：時ときを たずねる ときは whenを 使つかう [33]。When do you ...?は、「いつ…しますか」と たずねる ときに 使つかう [33]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use 'when' to ask about time [33]. 'When do you...?' asks for the specific time or day of an action [33].

grammarPoints.title: **Where is** the park? / **Where do you practice** on rainy days?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し（Where/前ぜん置ち詞し）：場ば所しょを たずねる ときは whereを 使つかう [34]。ものや 人ひとの 位いち置ちを 表あらわす ときは、下したのような 前ぜん置ち詞しを 使つかう [34]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use 'where' to ask about location [34]. Prepositions (like by, under, in, on) are used to indicate the location of things or people [34].

grammarPoints.title: **How many rabbits do you have**?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し（How many）：2ふたり人以い上じょうの 人ひとや 2つ以い上じょうの ものは、名めい詞しに sまたは esを つける [9]。 「いくつ」と 数かずを たずねる ときは how manyを 使つかい、後うしろに 名めい詞しの 複ふく数すう形けいを 続つづける [9]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When asking 'how many,' the question word 'how many' is followed by the plural form of the countable noun [9]. Countable nouns (two or more) typically take the -s or -es suffix [9].

grammarPoints.title: **What time is it**?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し（What time）：時じ刻こくを たずねる ときは What time is it?と 言いう [35]。相あい手てが 何なにかを する 時じ刻こくを たずねる ときは What time do you ...?と 言いう [36]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use 'What time is it?' to ask the current time [35]. Use 'What time do you...?' to ask the time when someone does something [36].
examples: **What time is it** in New Zealand?

grammarPoints.title: **What sports do you play**?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し（What + 名めい詞し）：疑ぎ問もん詞し Whatの あとに 名めい詞しを 続つづけ、What subjectや What sportsで 1つの かたまりに する [35]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When asking 'What kind of...' (e.g., what subject, what sports), the structure 〈What + Noun ...?〉 is used, forming one phrase [35].

grammarPoints.title: **Come to** the front.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 命めい令れい文ぶんと 助じょ言げん（動どう詞し原げん形けい）：人ひとに「…しなさい」という 指し示じや 助じょ言げんを する ときは、動どう詞しの もとの 形かたち（原げん形けい）で 文ぶんを 始はじめる [37]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To give instructions or advice, start the sentence with the base form of the verb (imperative form) [37].

grammarPoints.title: **Be** brave.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 命めい令れい文ぶんと 助じょ言げん（be動どう詞し）：静しずかに しなさい など、状じょう態たいを 示しめす 命めい令れい文ぶんは be動どう詞しの 原げん形けい beで 始はじめる [37]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: For commands that indicate a state (like 'be quiet'), start the sentence with the base form of the be-verb, 'Be' [37].

grammarPoints.title: **Don’t** worry.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 否ひ定ていの 命めい令れい文ぶんと 助じょ言げん：相あい手てに 「…を しないで」という 指し示じや 助じょ言げんを する ときは、動どう詞しの 前まえに don’tを つける [37]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To give negative instructions or advice ('Don't do...'), place 'Don't' before the verb [37].

grammarPoints.title: **Fumiya lives** in Hawaii.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 三さん人称にんしょう単たん数すう現げん在ざい形けい（肯こう定てい）：主しゅ語ごが I、you以い外がいで 単たん数すうの 場ば合あい、動どう詞しを sまたは esで 終おわる 形かたちに する [10]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When the subject is third person singular (He/She/It or singular name), the verb takes the -s or -es form [10]. This form is used to describe habits or current states.

grammarPoints.title: **Does Fumiya live** near a beach?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 三さん人称にんしょう単たん数すう現げん在ざい形けい（疑ぎ問もん文）：主しゅ語ごが I、you以い外がいで 単たん数すうの 場ば合あい、一いっ般ぱん動どう詞しの 疑ぎ問もん文ぶんでは 主しゅ語ごの 前まえに doesを 置おく [12]。このとき 動どう詞しには s、esを つけない [12]。答こたえの 文ぶんでは doesや does not [doesn’t]を 使つかう [12]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When forming a question in the third person singular, place 'does' before the subject [12], and the main verb uses its base form (no -s or -es) [12]. Responses use 'Yes, he does' or 'No, he does not (doesn't)' [12].
examples: **Does he go** to the beach every day?

grammarPoints.title: **Maria does not speak** Japanese.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 三さん人称にんしょう単たん数すう現げん在ざい形けい（否ひ定てい文）：主しゅ語ごが I、you以い外がいで 単たん数すうの 場ば合あい、否ひ定てい文ぶんでは 動どう詞しの 前まえに does not [doesn’t]が 入はいる [13]。このとき 動どう詞しには s、esを つけない [13]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: In negative sentences with a third person singular subject, place 'does not' (or 'doesn't') before the verb [13], and the main verb uses its base form [13].
examples: **The restaurant does not have** a website.

grammarPoints.title: That is Jun. **Do you know him**?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 代だい名めい詞し（目もく的てき格かく）：人ひとや ものを 動どう詞しの あとに 続つづけて「…を、…に」と 言いう ときは，me（私わたし）、you（あなた(たち)）、him（彼かれ）、her（彼かの女じょ）、them（彼かれら・彼かの女じょら・それら）を 使つかう [15]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When referring to people or things following a verb ('to whom,' 'who/what is affected'), use object pronouns (me, you, him, her, them) [15].
examples: **That is Anna. Do you know her?**

grammarPoints.title: **Whose ticket is this**? **It is mine**.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し（Whose/所しょ有ゆう代だい名めい詞し）：持もち主ぬしを たずねる ときには、whose（だれの）を 使つかう [16]。 「…の もの」と 答こたえる ときは、mine（私わたしの もの）やyours（あなたの もの）などが 使つかえる [16]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use 'whose' to ask about ownership [16]. To reply with ownership, use possessive pronouns like 'mine' or 'yours' [16].

grammarPoints.title: **Which do you speak**, English **or** Japanese?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し（Which）： 「どれ」「どちら」と たずねる ときには、whichを 使つかう [38]。 「Aですか、それとも Bですか」と たずねる ときには、A or B?で 表あらわす [38]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use 'which' when asking 'which one' or 'which of two options' [38]. To ask for a choice between two options, use 'A or B?' [38].
examples: **Which do you speak, English or Japanese?**

grammarPoints.title: **I am watching** TV now.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい進しん行こう形けい（肯こう定てい）：〈am [are, is] ＋ ...ing〉の 形かたちを 現げん在ざい進しん行こう形けいと いい、「...」の 動どう作さが ちょうど 今いま 進しん行こうしている ことを 表あらわす [17]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The present continuous form (am/is/are + -ing) indicates an action currently in progress [17]. This contrasts with the simple present tense which expresses habits [18, 39].

grammarPoints.title: **Are you walking** around a lake? / **What are people doing**?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい進しん行こう形けい（疑ぎ問もん文）：現げん在ざい進しん行こう形けいの 疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは、am、are、isを 主しゅ語ごの 前まえに 置おく [19]。複ふく数すうの 人ひとについて たずねる ときは What are people doing?と なる [19]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: For questions in the present continuous, place the be-verb (am, are, or is) before the subject [19]. To ask what multiple people are doing, use 'What are people doing?' [19].

grammarPoints.title: **How interesting!** **What a funny excuse!**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 感かん嘆たん文ぶん：〈How ＋ 形けい容よう詞し か副ふく詞し !〉または 〈What ＋ 名めい詞しを 含ふくむ語ご句く !〉で、「なんて…だろう！」と 感かん情じょうの 高たかぶりを 表あらわす [40]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Exclamatory sentences express strong emotion using either the structure 〈How + Adjective/Adverb!〉 or 〈What + Noun phrase!〉 [40].

grammarPoints.title: **She wants to help** people in need. / **She tries to do** her best.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 不ふ定てい詞し（名めい詞し的てき用よう法ほう）：wantや try、needなどの 動どう詞しの あとに 不ふ定てい詞し（to + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい）を 置おくと、「…する こと」や 「…である こと」といった 意い味みに なる [41]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Placing the infinitive (to + base verb) after verbs like *want, try, or need* means 'to do/be something' (noun usage of the infinitive) [41].

grammarPoints.title: **What do you want to eat**? / **I want to eat** chicken curry.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 不ふ定てい詞し（疑ぎ問もん文）：〈want [try, needなど] to + 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉は、このかたまりを 1つの 動どう詞しとして とらえる [42]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんや 否ひ定てい文ぶんの 作つくり方かたは、一いっ般ぱん動どう詞しの 場ば合あいと 同おなじ [42]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Phrases using an infinitive after verbs like *want, try, or need* are treated as a single verbal unit [42]. The formation of questions and negatives follows the rules for general verbs (using Do/Don't) [42].

grammarPoints.sectionName: Read and Think 4 (We Need Your Help!)
grammarPoints.title: The children **look happy**.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 動どう詞し（look）： 「…に 見みえる」という 話はなし手て（私わたし）の 視し覚かく的てきな 判はん断だんについて 言いう ときは、〈look + 形けい容よう詞し〉で 表あらわす [43]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To express the speaker's visual judgment ('...looks like...'), use the structure 〈look + adjective〉 [43].

grammarPoints.title: I **stayed** in Canada last winter. / I **went** to Canada during the winter vacation.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（過か去こ形けい 肯こう定てい）：すでに 終おわった ことを 表あらわす 場ば合あい、動どう詞しを 過か去こ形けいに する [20, 21]。規き則そく動どう詞しは edで 終おわり、不ふ規き則そく動どう詞しは 変へん化かする (went, saw, ateなど) [20]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To describe completed actions in the past, use the past tense form of the verb [20, 21]. Regular verbs add -ed, while irregular verbs change their form (e.g., go -> went) [20].
examples: **I saw** my favorite player in that game.

grammarPoints.title: **Did you eat** rice cakes?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（過か去こ形けい 疑ぎ問もん文）：過か去この 出で来き事ごとを たずねる 疑ぎ問もん文ぶんで、主しゅ語ごの 前まえに didを 置おく [22]。動どう詞しは 過か去こ形けいに しない [22]。答こたえの 文ぶんでは didや did not [didn’t]を 使つかう [22]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: For questions about past events, place 'did' before the subject [22], and the main verb uses its base form (not the past tense) [22]. Responses use 'Yes, I did' or 'No, I did not (didn't)' [22].

grammarPoints.sectionName: Read and Think 5 (New Year in Japan)
grammarPoints.title: I **did not buy** a good luck charm.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（過か去こ形けい 否ひ定てい文）：否ひ定てい文ぶんでは 動どう詞しの 前まえに did not [didn’t]を 置おく [23]。動どう詞しは 過か去こ形けいに しない [23]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: For negative statements in the past tense, place 'did not' (or 'didn't') before the verb [23], and the main verb uses its base form [23].
examples: **I did not buy** a good luck charm.
**I did not have** a bad time.

grammarPoints.title: **Were you nervous** during the contest?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: be動どう詞し（過か去こ形けい 疑ぎ問もん文）：amや isの 過か去こ形けいは wasに、areの 過か去こ形けいは wereに なる [24]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは be動どう詞し 過か去こ形けいを 主しゅ語ごの 前まえに 置おく [24]。was notは wasn’tに、were notは weren’tに 短たん縮しゅくできる [24]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The past tense of 'am/is' is 'was'; 'are' is 'were' [24]. Questions are formed by inverting the past tense be-verb and the subject [24]. Contractions (wasn't, weren't) can be used for negation [24].

grammarPoints.title: I **was playing** soccer then.
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 過か去こ進しん行こう形けい：過か去この ある 時じ点てんに していた ことを 表あらわすには、〈was [were] + ...ing〉を 使つかう [25, 26]。この 形かたちを 過か去こ進しん行こう形けいと いう [25]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To express an action that was in progress at a specific point in the past, use the past continuous form 〈was [were] + ...ing〉 [25, 26].

grammarPoints.title: **There is** a campground near the lake. / **Is there** a campground near the lake?
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: There is [are] 構こう文ぶん：「…が ある［いる］」と 言いう 場ば合あいは There is [are] ....を 使つかう [44]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは Is [Are] there ...?と なり [44]、否ひ定てい的てきな 答こたえは No, there isn’t [aren’t].と 短たん縮しゅくできる [44]。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use 'There is [are]...' to state that something exists or is located somewhere [44]. For questions, use 'Is [Are] there...?' [44]. Negative responses can use contractions (isn't/aren't) [44].
examples: **There were** many students around the campfire.

grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The verb 'am' acts as a be-verb, connecting the words before and after it [1]. 'I am' can be contracted to 'I'm' [1]. This is used to state identity or status.

grammarPoint.title: I **like** Japanese sweets.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（肯こう定てい文）：動どう作さや 状じょう態たいを 表あらわす 場ば合あいは、主しゅ語ごの 後うしろに playや likeなどの 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞しが 入はいる [1]。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: When expressing actions or states, a general verb such as 'play' or 'like' is placed after the subject [1]. This is used to express habitual actions or current states.

exercises.question: I / like / Japanese / sweets.
exercises.hint: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（肯こう定てい文）：動どう作さや 状じょう態たいを 表あらわす 場ば合あいは、主しゅ語ごの 後うしろに playや likeなどの 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞しが 入はいる。

exercises.question: I ___ soccer.

exercises.question: play / I / tennis

exercises.question: I ___ music.

exercises.question: play / I / the / piano

exercises.question: I ___ a dog.

exercises.translation: 私は犬を飼っています。

grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: be動どう詞し（過か去こ形けい 疑ぎ問もん文）：amや isの 過か去こ形けいは wasに、areの 過か去こ形けいは wereに なる [24]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは be動どう詞し 過か去こ形けいを 主しゅ語ごの 前まえに 置おく [24]。was notは wasn’tに、were notは weren’tに 短たん縮しゅくできる [24]。

grammarPoint.title: **There is** a campground near the lake. / **Is there** a campground near the lake?
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: There is [are] 構こう文ぶん：「…が ある［いる］」と 言いう 場ば合あいは There is [are] ....を 使つかう [44]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは Is [Are] there ...?と なり [44]、否ひ定てい的てきな 答こたえは No, there isn’t [aren’t].と 短たん縮しゅくできる [44]。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: Use 'There is [are]...' to state that something exists or is located somewhere [44]. For questions, use 'Is [Are] there...?' [44]. Negative responses can use contractions (isn't/aren't) [44].
examples: **There were** many students around the campfire.

grammarPoint.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 4: 三さん人称にんしょう単たん数すう現げん在ざい形けい
grammarPoint.title: **Fumiya lives** in Hawaii. / **Does Fumiya live** near a beach? / **Maria does not speak** Japanese.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 三さん人称にんしょう単たん数すう現げん在ざい形けい：主しゅ語ごが I、you以い外がいで 単たん数すうの 場ば合あい、動どう詞しを sまたは esで 終おわる 形かたちに する [10, 11]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは doesを 主しゅ語ごの 前まえに 置おき、動どう詞しに s、esを つけない [11, 12]。否ひ定てい文ぶんは does not [doesn't]を 動どう詞しの 前まえに 入いれ、動どう詞しに s、esを つけない [11, 13]。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: When the subject is third person singular, the verb takes -s or -es in affirmatives [10, 11]. For questions, use 'does' before the subject (verb is base form) [11, 12]. For negation, use 'does not/doesn't' before the verb (verb is base form) [11, 13].
examples: **Does he go** to the beach every day?

grammarPoint.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 3: 名めい詞し
grammarPoint.title: **How many rabbits do you have**?
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 名めい詞し（数かずえ方かた）：人ひとや ものの 名な前まえを 表あらわす 語ごを 名めい詞しと いう [7]。2ふたり人以い上じょうの 人ひとや 2つ以い上じょうの ものは、多おおくの 場ば合あい、名めい詞しに sまたは esを つける [8, 9]。数かずえられない 名めい詞し（water、meatなど）は a[an]が ついたり、sで 終おわる 形かたちにはならない [7]。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: Nouns name people or things [7]. Countable nouns (two or more) usually take the plural form (-s or -es) [8, 9]. Uncountable nouns (materials, abstract things) do not take 'a/an' or typically use the plural form ending in -s [7].

grammarPoint.title: **Were you nervous** during the contest?
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: be動どう詞し（過か去こ形けい）：amや isの 過か去こ形けいは wasに、areの 過か去こ形けいは wereに なる [24]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは be動どう詞し 過か去こ形けいを 主しゅ語ごの 前まえに 置おく [24]。was notは wasn’tに、were notは weren’tに 短たん縮しゅくできる [24].
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The past tense of 'am/is' is 'was'; 'are' is 'were' [24]. Questions are formed by placing the past tense be-verb before the subject [24]. Contractions (wasn't, weren't) can be used for negation [24].

grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 過か去こ進しん行こう形けい：過か去この ある 時じ点てんに していた ことを 表あらわすには、〈was [were] + ...ing〉を 使つかう [25, 26]。この 形かたちを 過か去こ進しん行こう形けいと いう [25].

grammarPoint.title: **I am watching** TV now. / **Are you walking** around a lake? / **What are people doing**?
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 現げん在ざい進しん行こう形けい：〈am [are, is] ＋ ...ing〉の 形かたちを 現げん在ざい進しん行こう形けいと いい、「...」の 動どう作さが ちょうど 今いま 進しん行こうしている ことを 表あらわす [17, 18]。疑ぎ問もん文ぶんは、am、are、isを 主しゅ語ごの 前まえに 置おく [19].
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) expresses an action happening right now [17, 18]. For questions, invert the subject and the be-verb (Are you...?) [19].

grammarPoint.sectionName: Grammar for Communication 5: 代だい名めい詞し
grammarPoint.title: **Do you know him**? / **Whose ticket is this**? **It is mine**.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 代だい名めい詞し：一いち度ど 話わ題だいに 出でた 名めい詞しのかわりを する 語ごを 代だい名めい詞しと いう [14]。人ひとや ものを 動どう詞しの あとに 続つづけて「…を、…に」と 言いう ときは，me（私わたし）、you（あなた(たち)）、him（彼かれ）、her（彼かの女じょ）、them（彼かれら・彼かの女じょら・それら）を 使つかう [15].
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: Pronouns replace nouns already mentioned [14]. Use objective pronouns (me, him, her, them) after a verb ('to whom,' 'who/what is affected') [15]. Possessive pronouns (mine, yours) are used to indicate ownership [16].
examples: **That is Anna. Do you know her?**
**Whose bag is this? It is mine.**

grammarPoint.title: **I stayed** in Canada last winter. / **I went** to Canada during the winter vacation.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 一いっ般ぱん動どう詞し（過か去こ形けい 肯こう定てい）：すでに 終おわった ことを 表あらわす 場ば合あい、動どう詞しを 過か去こ形けいに する [20, 21]。規き則そく動どう詞しは edで 終おわり、不ふ規き則そく動どう詞しは 変へん化かする (went, saw, ateなど) [20].
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: To describe completed actions in the past, use the past tense form of the verb [20, 21]. Regular verbs add -ed, while irregular verbs change forms (e.g., go -> went) [20].

grammarPoint.title: **Did you eat** rice cakes? / **I did not buy** a good luck charm.
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 過か去こ形けい 疑ぎ問もん文ぶんと 否ひ定てい文ぶん：疑ぎ問もん文ぶんで、主しゅ語ごの 前まえに didを 置おき [22]，動どう詞しは 過か去こ形けいに しない [22]。否ひ定てい文ぶんは 動どう詞しの 前まえに did not [didn’t]を 置おく [23]。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: For past tense questions, place 'did' before the subject (verb is base form) [22]. For negative statements, place 'did not/didn't' before the verb (verb is base form) [23].
examples: **I did not buy** a good luck charm.

grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 英えい語ごの 文ぶんの 基き本ほん的てきな 語ご順じゅんは、〈 **主しゅ語ご** （…は・が） ＋ **動どう詞し** （…する・です） ＋ その他たの語ご句く 〉です。
